chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Hamad al-Khazzaz, from Abd al-Aziz al-Qaratisi, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abd al-Aziz! Indeed, faith (Iman) consists of ten ranks, like a ladder from which one ascends step by step. So do not say to the one who has two ranks, 'You are nothing,' until he reaches the tenth. And do not dismiss those who are below you, lest the one who is above you dismiss you. When you see someone who is lower than you, raise him to you gently, and do not burden him with what he cannot bear, lest you break him. Indeed, whoever breaks a believer must repair him. Al-Miqdad was in the eighth rank, Abu Dharr in the ninth, and Salman in the tenth.'
ai.seo_question: What are the ten ranks of faith (Iman) and how should believers treat each other according to their spiritual levels?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that faith consists of ten hierarchical ranks, using the metaphor of a ladder to illustrate spiritual progression. He cautions against the arrogance of those higher in rank dismissing those lower, and against the negligence of those higher towards those below, emphasizing gentle mentorship to avoid causing spiritual fracture. This teaching underscores the Shia concept of *tadaruj* (gradualism) in faith, where each level is valid and necessary, rather than a binary state of belief.
